intro: In a letter–number analogy, letters are turned into numbers (or other letters) by a rule. Find the rule from the first pair, then use it on the second.

tips.title: Write the places under the letters
tips.body: Put A = 1 … Z = 26 under each letter. Most of these questions are about those numbers, not the letters themselves.

tips.title: One letter, one number? Think squares
tips.body: If a single letter goes to a big number, check its square and the square of its neighbour: M = 13, and 196 = 14².

tips.title: A word and a number? Add the places
tips.body: Add up the places of the word's letters. Then see how the total became the number: the same, doubled, halved, squared or square-rooted.

tips.title: Letters to letters? Find each step
tips.body: Write the step under each letter (+2, +3, +4…). The steps often grow, or go up and down in turn.

tips.title: Opposite letters add up to 27
tips.body: A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, C ↔ X … A letter's opposite is 27 minus its place: D (4) → 23, which is W.

tips.title: Check every option
tips.body: Long codes often differ in just one or two letters. Work out the whole answer first, then compare it letter by letter.
